python3 - <<'PY'

Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+p.extract_text() for i,p in enumerate(r.pages)))

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant failure mode of classifier-based Bayesian optimization. Combining BORE-style acquisition with label propagation or label spreading is a plausible, potentially useful contribution, particularly when candidate pools provide meaningful geometric information.

The experiments show encouraging gains, especially on synthetic functions and NATS-Bench. Comparisons include multiple BORE/LFBO classifiers and GP baselines, with 20 repetitions and reported standard errors.

The appendices provide substantial sensitivity analyses covering kernel bandwidth, unlabeled sample counts, sampling distributions, threshold ratios, and pool subsampling. The relationship to established density-ratio estimation and semi-supervised learning methods is generally clear.
weaknesses: The central benefit attributable to semi-supervised learning is insufficiently isolated. Figure 12 includes a valuable no-transduction control, but it sometimes matches or outperforms SSL, and this experiment fixes beta at 0.5 whereas the main results learn beta. Matched-bandwidth controls and separate ablations of propagation, bandwidth learning, and random tie-breaking are needed to establish which component produces the gains. This unresolved attribution is the main reason for my weak-reject recommendation.

The explanation for improved exploration remains heuristic. Sampling truncated Gaussians around evaluated points does not establish Assumption 4.1: high-density connections need not respect objective-derived labels. Expanding the predicted favorable region also does not necessarily improve exploration when acquisition selection still maximizes class probability. Appendix D acknowledges that the cited i.i.d. learning guarantees do not directly apply to the adaptive optimization setting.

The comparisons do not sufficiently test alternative remedies for the motivating failure mode. Simple randomized exploration and regularized or uncertainty-aware BORE/LFBO classifiers would help determine whether transduction provides an advantage over simpler interventions. It is also unclear whether the flat-landscape tie-breaking heuristic is applied consistently to competing classifiers.

Evidence for general applicability is limited. All continuous synthetic benchmarks are two-dimensional. The 64-dimensional MNIST representation is trained on 440,000 labeled examples to predict the same three-digit quantity being optimized. Although the embeddings are shared across methods, this primarily tests search in an objective-informed representation and provides limited evidence for general high-dimensional black-box optimization.

Important implementation details remain unspecified, including the label-spreading clamping value, propagation stopping settings, and bandwidth-optimization initialization and bounds. The general L-BFGS-B description also does not explain how acquisition maximization respects fixed-pool feasibility, particularly for MNIST embeddings. These omissions matter given the demonstrated parameter sensitivity.

A smaller mathematical correction is needed in Section 4.1: the column-normalized definition of p_ij implies P = W D^{-1}, whereas the text states P = D^{-1} W before using P transpose in Equation 11. The intended normalization and update should be made consistent.
